**Summary of what I did and why**

I researched Apple's most recent results on the web (Apple Newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR) and checked the live quote, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.90 (quote was $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask at 15:05 UTC, so the limit was ~0.1% above market and the order filled immediately for a total of $8,916 — inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well within today's $20,000 total, with cash of $50,000 available and no money moved out of the account). The thesis: Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year — an acceleration in growth — capping a fiscal year with total net sales of $391.0 billion, operating income of $123.2 billion, net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 (FY2023: $6.13), the EPS dip being attributable to a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge rather than operating deterioration, while operating cash flow of $118.3 billion confirms the underlying earnings power and supports continued buybacks/dividends. Qualitative catalysts (Apple Intelligence rollout with iOS 18.1, holiday-quarter iPhone cycle, services at record levels) support holding a moderate position, while the main risks are a rich multiple (~37x FY24 EPS) and continued softness in Greater China. Note the open-web search tool returned very limited third-party coverage today (only Apple's own newsroom and the SEC filing were reachable; one result block was quarantined by the security screen and ignored), so my decision rests on those primary filings plus the broker quote rather than analyst commentary. This is a starter-sized position; I did not touch the existing 100 MSFT shares.
